title: A tile map from text
description:
Load a level from text and ask what is at any position.

```
##########
#P....C..#
#..###...#
#......E.#
##########
player at tile (1, 1), 1 coin, 1 enemy
pixel (48, 20) -> tile (3, 1) -> empty
pixel (64, 40) -> tile (4, 2) -> wall
```
hints: `int tx{static_cast<int>(std::floor(px / 16))};` and the same for y; check both are inside the rows before indexing (lesson 4.02).
Loop over every character once when loading, replacing `P`, `C` and `E` with `.` after recording them.
requirements: Tiles are 16 pixels; `#` wall, `.` empty, and letters for things to place.
Things are taken out of the map into a list; their tile becomes empty.
`tileAt(px, py)` treats anything outside the map as a wall.
stretch: Load the same level from a Tiled `.tmj` JSON export. The course does not teach reading JSON: look up a JSON library such as nlohmann/json (available through vcpkg) and Tiled's documentation of the map's `layers` and `data` fields.
